# 1 Clement Chapter 51 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 51 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_051_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 51

**51:1** For whatever we have done wrong, for whatever the adversary has manipulated us into doing — let us seek forgiveness. And those who have set themselves up as leaders of this rebellion ought to fix their eyes on the hope we all share.

**51:2** People who live in the fear and love of God would rather suffer themselves than let their neighbors suffer. They would rather face condemnation themselves than see the beautiful harmony of the community — so faithfully handed down to us — brought into disgrace.

**51:3** It is far better to confess your sin than to harden your heart. Remember what happened to those who rebelled against Moses, the servant of God — their judgment was plain for all to see.

**51:4** They went down alive into the realm of the dead, and "Death became their shepherd."

**51:5** And then there was Pharaoh himself — with all his army, all Egypt's rulers, the chariots and their drivers — all swallowed up in the Red Sea and destroyed. Why? Simply because their foolish hearts were hardened, even after God had performed all those signs and wonders in Egypt through his servant Moses.

---

*PNEUMA renders for contemporary clarity and accessibility, capturing the spirit of Clement's pastoral appeal.*
